ai.literal: The false conduct of him who has a deceitful mind, the five elements within indeed will laugh.
ai.translation: At the false conduct of a man with a deceitful mind, the five elements that dwell within him will laugh in derision.
ai.modern: வஞ்சக மனதை உடையவனுடைய பொய்யான ஒழுக்கத்தைக் கண்டு, அவனுடைய உடம்பிற்குள் இருக்கும் ஐந்து பூதங்களும் மனதிற்குள் சிரிக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the futility of hypocrisy. A person may successfully deceive the outside world with a false show of virtuous conduct (படிற்றொழுக்கம்). However, they cannot hide their true nature from the five elements (பூதங்கள் ஐந்தும்)—earth, water, fire, air, and space—that constitute their own physical body. Knowing the inner deceit, these elements laugh inwardly (அகத்தே நகும்) at the hypocrite's pretense, emphasizing that true virtue must be genuine and internal.

ai.literal: Sky-high appearance what will it do, if one's own mind falls into guilt known to oneself?
ai.translation: Of what use is an imposing, sky-high appearance of holiness if one's own mind is conscious of a sin committed?
ai.modern: தன் நெஞ்சம் அறிய ஒருவன் தவறு செய்வானானால், அவனுடைய வானளவு உயர்ந்த தவக்கோலம் அவனுக்கு என்ன நன்மையைச் செய்யும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the emptiness of external religious or ascetic posturing when unaccompanied by inner purity. The poet asks what benefit a 'sky-high appearance' (வானுயர் தோற்றம்)—referring to the grand outward garb or posture of an ascetic—can possibly bring if the person's own conscience (தன்னெஞ்சம்) is fully aware of a hidden sin (தான்அறி குற்றம்) they have committed. True virtue is defined by the purity of the mind, and outward displays cannot mask or cure a guilty conscience.

words.gloss: he who has the state of mind

ai.literal: A person who has a state of being without strength of self-control, adopting a severe guise, is like a cow grazing after wrapping itself in a tiger's skin.
ai.translation: The severe ascetic guise assumed by a man who lacks the strength of self-control is like a cow grazing on crops while wrapped in a tiger's skin.
ai.modern: மனவலிமை இல்லாத ஒருவன் தவக்கோலம் பூண்டு ஒழுக்கமற்று வாழ்வது, ஒரு பசு மாடு புலியின் தோலைப் போர்த்திக் கொண்டு பயிரை மேய்வதைப் போன்றது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to expose the hypocrisy of those who pretend to be ascetics but lack inner self-control. The poet compares a person without mental strength who puts on a powerful ascetic appearance to a cow that covers itself with a tiger's skin to graze on crops. Just as the cow uses the tiger's skin to scare away the farmers so it can feed on their fields without being stopped, the hypocritical ascetic uses the respected garb of renunciation to indulge in forbidden desires without being questioned. Ultimately, both the cow's disguise and the false ascetic's guise are deceptive covers for their true, weak natures.

words.gloss: hiding behind the guise of penance

ai.literal: Hiding behind penance, doing evil deeds, is like a hunter hiding behind a bush and trapping birds.
ai.translation: Performing evil deeds while hiding behind the guise of penance is like a hunter hiding behind a bush to trap birds.
ai.modern: தவ வேடத்திற்குப் பின்னால் மறைந்து கொண்டு தீய செயல்களைச் செய்வது, ஒரு வேடன் புதருக்குப் பின்னால் மறைந்து பறவைகளைப் பிடிப்பதற்கு ஒப்பானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid simile to expose the hypocrisy of those who pretend to be ascetics while committing sins. The poet compares a false ascetic to a hunter. Just as a hunter hides behind a bush (புதல்) to deceive and trap unsuspecting birds (புள்), a hypocrite uses the outward appearance of penance (தவம்) as a shield to perform evil deeds (அல்லவை) without being suspected. The key words 'தவமறைந்து' (hiding behind penance) and 'புதல்மறைந்து' (hiding behind a bush) draw a direct parallel between religious hypocrisy and predatory deception.

ai.literal: The deceitful conduct of those who say 'We are without attachment' will bring many ruins, saying 'Alas! Alas!'
ai.translation: The false conduct of those who claim, 'We have renounced all attachments,' will bring them many miseries, making them cry out in deep regret, 'Alas, what have I done!'
ai.modern: பற்றுக்களைத் துறந்துவிட்டோம் என்று கூறுபவர்களின் வஞ்சகமான ஒழுக்கம், 'ஐயோ! ஐயோ!' என்று அவர்கள் வருந்தும்படி பல துன்பங்களைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the hypocrisy of false ascetics who pretend to have renounced all worldly desires while secretly indulging in them. The word 'படிற்று' means deceitful or false, and 'ஒழுக்கம்' refers to conduct. The phrase 'எற்று எற்று' is an exclamation of intense grief and regret ('Alas! Alas!'). The poet emphasizes that such deceitful behavior will eventually be exposed, bringing numerous miseries ('ஏதம் பலவும்') that will make the hypocrites lament their actions in deep sorrow.

ai.literal: Than those who live deceiving like those who have renounced, while not renouncing in their mind, hard-hearted people there are none.
ai.translation: There are no people more hard-hearted than those who, without renouncing worldly desires in their minds, live deceiving others by posing as true ascetics.
ai.modern: மனதால் பற்றுகளைத் துறக்காமல், துறந்தவர்களைப் போல நடித்துப் பிறரை ஏமாற்றி வாழ்பவர்களை விடக் கொடிய நெஞ்சமுடையவர்கள் வேறு யாரும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet addresses the severe hypocrisy of false ascetics. The phrase 'நெஞ்சின் துறவார்' refers to those who still harbor worldly desires in their hearts, while 'துறந்தார்போல்' describes their outward pretense of having renounced everything. The poet emphasizes that there are no individuals more ruthless or hard-hearted ('வன்கணார் இல்') than these pretenders, as they weaponize a sacred way of life solely to deceive others for personal gain.

words.gloss: those who are like what is seen

ai.literal: Even if they are like the outside of a crab's eye seed, the world possesses those who are black inside like its tip.
ai.translation: Though they appear as bright red as the outside of a crab's eye seed, the world contains those whose hearts are as black as that seed's tip.
ai.modern: வெளியே குன்றிமணியின் சிவந்த நிறத்தைப் போல நல்லவர்களாகக் தோன்றினாலும், உள்ளே அக்குன்றிமணியின் மூக்கைப் போலக் கரிய மனமுடையவர்களை இவ்வுலகம் கொண்டுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the striking image of the 'kunri' seed (crab's eye seed) to expose hypocrites who practice false asceticism. The seed is brilliantly red and beautiful on the outside, but has a distinct black spot at its tip. Similarly, some people appear pure, virtuous, and radiant on the outside, but their inner minds are filled with dark, evil thoughts. The poet warns that the world contains such deceptive individuals, urging us to look beyond outward appearances.

words.gloss: that which is in the mind

ai.literal: That which is in the mind being impurity, bathing in water like great people, hiding themselves and conducting themselves, people are many.
ai.translation: There are many who, while their minds are filled with impurity, bathe in water like noble ascetics, hiding their true nature and conducting themselves falsely.
ai.modern: மனதில் உள்ளவை குற்றமாக இருக்க, உயர்ந்தவர்களைப் போல நீரில் மூழ்கி நீராடி, தம் தீய ஒழுக்கத்தை மறைத்து வாழும் மனிதர்கள் பலர் உள்ளனர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet exposes the hypocrisy of false ascetics who pretend to be pure. While their minds remain filled with impurities and evil thoughts, they perform external rituals like bathing in sacred waters to mimic the behavior of truly noble souls. Under this guise of holiness, they hide their true character and conduct themselves deceitfully. The poet emphasizes that external purification is meaningless without internal purity, and warns that many such impostors exist in society.

ai.literal: The arrow is cruel (though straight); the lute's neck is righteous (though curved); in that same manner, judge people by the nature of their actions.
ai.translation: An arrow is straight but deadly, while the lute's neck is curved but produces sweet music. Likewise, judge people by the nature of their actions, not by their outward appearance.
ai.modern: அம்பு நேராக இருந்தாலும் கொடியது; யாழின் தண்டு வளைந்திருந்தாலும் நன்மையானது. அதுபோலவே, மனிதர்களை அவர்களுடைய தோற்றத்தை வைத்து மதிப்பிடாமல், அவர்கள் செய்யும் செயல்களின் தன்மையைக் கொண்டு மதிப்பிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against judging people solely by their outward appearance or behavior. The poet uses two vivid analogies: an arrow, which is perfectly straight but is used to kill, and a lute (yāḻ), whose neck is bent but produces beautiful, harmonious music. Just as straightness does not guarantee goodness and crookedness does not imply evil in objects, a person's external form or feigned righteousness can be deceptive. Therefore, one must evaluate others based on the actual quality and consequences of their actions ('viṉaipaṭu pālāl').

ai.literal: Shaving [the head] and growing [the hair] long are not required, if [one] completely avoids that which the world condemns.
ai.translation: There is no need for shaving the head or growing the hair long, if one completely avoids those actions that the world condemns.
ai.modern: உலகம் பழிக்கும் செயல்களைத் தவிர்த்துவிட்டால், தலையை மழிப்பதோ அல்லது முடியை வளர்ப்பதோ தேவையில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet concludes the chapter on inconsistent conduct by highlighting that external symbols of asceticism are meaningless without inner discipline. The poet states that shaving one's head or growing one's hair long—common outward signs of renunciation—are entirely unnecessary. What truly matters is the internal restraint to avoid actions that are condemned by wise people in the world. True renunciation lies in the purity of conduct, not in external appearances.
